note: Declarative mapping from the Hermes/Personal-Agent sources to the six bundled Professor skills. Each check is two-sided: `sourceAnchor` must match the SOURCE file (proving the behaviour exists upstream) and `pluginPattern` must match the PLUGIN skill (proving it was carried over). A source whose anchor no longer matches means the upstream rule changed and the port must be re-reviewed: the verifier fails rather than silently drifting.

placeholders.${PERSONAL_AGENT_ROOT}: the dependency workspace that holds the learning-agent sources

portability.rule: A bundled skill may name a Hermes / Personal-Agent location only inside a `## …` section whose heading contains "Optional", where it is an explicit, user-initiated import of pre-existing data. Everywhere else the skill addresses Professor-owned state (`.professor/…`) through `professor_*` tools. `verify-skill-sync.mjs` enforces this against the delivered text.

professor-course-management: Optional: importing an existing Personal-Agent registry

divergences: The upstream registry is a pair of Markdown files (COURSES.md + per-course COURSES_TEMPLATE-derived files) that the agent edits directly; Professor owns the same table inside `.professor/project.yaml` and only ever writes it through `professor_course_manage`. The upstream file names therefore no longer appear in a mandatory section — `COURSE_TEMPLATE.md` vs the real `COURSES_TEMPLATE.md` is now historical, because there is no template file at all.
The Knowledge Root is derived (`.professor/state/courses/<course_id>/`) instead of configured, so the registry field became a resolved location rather than an input.
Upstream splits course management across one skill; here it is one skill with the same operation names (REGISTER/SYNC/LOCATE/UPDATE/ARCHIVE).
The legacy Registry import moved into an explicitly Optional section: it is an explicit, user-initiated workflow, never part of a fresh install.

The directory contract distinguishes rebuildable indexes from persistent learning state and saved artifacts. Actual note/review fallback roots and the explicit per-artifact format gate supersede obsolete upstream assumptions.
Course AI-Notes output must be confirmed and passed as notes_root during registration; omission uses the project fallback, and the current update action does not accept notes_root.

checks.label: lightweight questions take no state write

divergences: Upstream splits the mode catalogue (MODES.md) from the session workflow (study-session); the plugin merges them into one skill because the preset exposes a single study entry point.
Algorithm Coach guidance is deliberately absent: for this workspace the user scoped the plugin to the course Professor, and Algorithm Coach is a separate bot.

The plugin adds its own bounded material-reading workflow: plan, source text, optional local OCR/structure enhancement, PDF images and session notes before teaching; runtime readiness and vision limits are explicit.

First-use PDF enhancement prepares a workspace-scoped runtime with shipped platform locks and model hashes; setup needs host Python 3.12 and network, while recognition is offline. Honest source absence and image interpretation were checked with the configured model.

2026-10-12 teaching-interaction update: request-intent handling (complete explanation / incremental tutoring / understanding check / hint-only), a graduated assistance ladder, optional targeted understanding checks, first-gap feedback with an error taxonomy, and assistance-aware evidence wording were added as original Professor text implementing docs/qa/2026-10-11-teaching-design/RESEARCH.md. The design was informed by four open-source skill repositories recorded there (bstellato/ai-teaching-skills MIT, learning-commons-org/agent-skills Apache-2.0, Jellypod-Inc/school-skills MIT, GarethManning/education-agent-skills CC BY-SA 4.0); no third-party wording was copied or adapted, so the two-sided checks above still verify the originally ported behaviours only.

2026-10-14: meaningful explanation depth is explicit near the start: prerequisites and notation, justified derivation, a worked example, usable knowledge connections, conditions/boundaries and transfer. Ordinary short lesson requests retain this depth; explicit brief/hint/check/translation requests keep their scope. The progressive default is deeper (version 2); existing saved preferences are not migrated or overwritten.

2026-10-14 readable-layout follow-up: continuous step bridges, semantic H1/H2 heading hierarchy, selective bold and labelled cues, render-aware plain mathematics for unknown/failed viewers, truthful table/tree/image visuals, and escaped literal bars inside Markdown table cells. Progressive preset version 3 carries this presentation preference; host CSS, permissions and saved snapshots remain unchanged.

checks.label: notes never land in Knowledge
checks.pluginPattern: Never write final notes into the Knowledge

divergences: The upstream skill also owns the study-mode teaching text; that moved to `professor-study` so this skill only covers artifacts.
Upstream could reuse a concrete registry default. The later approved plugin rule supersedes that behavior: every artifact needs an explicit format choice for the current request.

The format gate follows the previously approved runtime contract: a saved default never bypasses an explicit format choice for the current artifact. Creation is routed through the bundled professor_artifact_create tool and checked against created/files.

The skill resolves actual output roots through artifact_status, reads missing source bodies through material_read, and explicitly registers an index entry only after successful creation; INDEX remains a separate host filesystem edit, not an artifact or state_update side effect.

2026-10-14: ordinary review notes preserve definitions, intermediate reasoning, worked examples, prerequisite connections and conditions so they stand alone. Explicit summaries/formula sheets remain compact. Supplementary reasoning is labelled and note generation still provides no mastery evidence; format, output and provenance contracts are unchanged.

2026-10-14 readable-layout follow-up: preserve heading hierarchy already provided by the artifact tool, avoid duplicate titles, keep derivation bridges and selective emphasis, match math/visual syntax to the actual viewer, and escape literal vertical bars in pipe-table cells. Explicit summaries/formula sheets remain scoped; arbitrary HTML color or diagram source is not claimed as a rendered asset.

2026-10-15: explicit body_tex fragments in sections/examples/review derivations are the preferred one-pass LaTeX route; prose body remains escaped, generated-copy host edits remain repair/integration fallback. Fragment validation does not establish correct math or successful typesetting. Environment failure_class stops document repairs; visual coverage is reported from actual pages. Inspection-only reuse requires returned reused_prior_compile true, proving unchanged source fingerprint and actual PDF hash rather than an assumed no-change state.
Review behaviour lives in the Hermes persona (SOUL.md), not in a Personal-Agent skill; it therefore has no Personal-Agent source counterpart, and the plugin makes it an explicit on-demand skill.
The review artifact is written as a separate file rather than appended to lecture notes, matching the upstream rule that it must not overwrite ordinary notes.

Review uses bundled course/state/material tools, reports absent state honestly, saves only when requested, and resolves the review output root rather than assuming the lecture-note root. Practice origins and creation evidence follow artifact_create.

divergences: The template is no longer assumed to exist. Upstream always copied a shared default template from the dependency workspace (${PERSONAL_AGENT_ROOT}/06_Shared/Templates/LaTeX/Course-Notes/Default/); the plugin resolves the course's configured LaTeX Template when it names a real directory and otherwise generates a self-contained project, so a fresh install with no template library still produces a compilable note.
The shared note format gate requires an explicit LaTeX choice for the current artifact, consistent with professor-notes and the runtime tool; saved defaults do not bypass it.

The bundled artifact and latex_compile tools are the operational authority: the fallback has main.tex/content.tex/professor-metadata.tex, metadata uses Professor-prefixed macros, tool text inputs are escaped, and the skill inspects/edits only the generated copy before a bounded compilation repair loop. Compilation and PDF inspection remain separate evidence.

2026-10-15: the self-contained default now reads bundled resources/latex/default/main.tex, adapted from the user-supplied CSC3001note2.tex, with a verbatim reference shipped separately. The default preserves dual large titles, separator and compact paragraphs; adds portable XeLaTeX/Fandol CJK, larger semantic headings, named emphasis boxes and original diagram/code facilities; uses course/request metadata instead of the reference identity. Explicit usable custom templates retain precedence. Skill documentation names actual default facilities and keeps generated-copy editing and independent compile/visual gates.

2026-10-15: explicit body_tex fragments in sections/examples/review derivations are the preferred one-pass LaTeX route; prose body remains escaped, generated-copy host edits remain repair/integration fallback. Fragment validation does not establish correct math or successful typesetting. Environment failure_class stops document repairs; visual coverage is reported from actual pages. Inspection-only reuse requires returned reused_prior_compile true, proving unchanged source fingerprint and actual PDF hash rather than an assumed no-change state.
